finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unvalidated req.query.host is concatenated into a shell command string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters in host execute arbitrary commands and the output is returned to the caller.
finding.source: req.query.host from the HTTP query string (GET /ping?host=...), read at tools.js:6-7

trace.note: app.get("/ping") registers the route for any unauthenticated request
"ping -c 1 " + req.query.host concatenates raw input into a shell string
exec passes the string to /bin/sh -c, so ';', '|', '&&', backticks, $() and newlines are interpreted; e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id runs id
res.send(out) returns stdout, giving the attacker direct output

finding.guards_checked: No validation (no net.isIP or hostname regex or allowlist); no escaping; execFile with argv not used; no auth middleware; Express query arrays (host[]=a&host[]=b) still join and inject; only a missing host is non-injectable. Drive-by variant: no CORS or Origin checks, so a malicious web page can trigger GET localhost:3001/ping?host=... and the command runs even though the response is unreadable. Verified by reading only, not executed.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only file is tools.js. The /ping route (tools.js:6) has no auth middleware, and host is concatenated raw into the string passed to exec() (tools.js:7), which runs via /bin/sh -c. No net.isIP, regex, allowlist, or escaping is present. The err branch (tools.js:8-9) only affects the response, not whether the command runs. res.send(out) (tools.js:11) returns stdout to the caller. The app has no CORS middleware, so the drive-by variant needs no preflight for a simple GET.
verdict.reason: Any anonymous client can send GET /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id, and tools.js:7 passes the unvalidated string to exec(), which runs the injected command under /bin/sh with its output returned via tools.js:11, with no guard anywhere in the code.

finding.claim: No authentication or authorization on any route, and the server binds to all interfaces by default, exposing command execution (F1) and host info to anyone who can reach port 3001.
finding.source: Any network peer that can reach port 3001, or any web page via the browser drive-by in F1
finding.sink: exec() at tools.js:7 (command execution) and exec('uptime') at tools.js:25; /version discloses git HEAD at tools.js:16-20

trace.note: app.listen(3001) with no host argument binds to 0.0.0.0
/version has no auth and reveals the git HEAD hash of the server's working repo
/uptime has no auth and reveals host uptime

finding.guards_checked: No auth, IP filtering, or Origin checks exist in the file. Any reverse proxy or firewall outside this file was not verifiable.

verdict.guard_found: none. No auth middleware, IP filtering, or Origin check exists in tools.js. The routes at tools.js:6, :15, and :24 are registered bare, and app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 has no host argument. The only other checks are error-status returns at tools.js:8-10, :17-19, which are not access controls.
verdict.reason: Every route (tools.js:6, :15, :24) is registered without any auth check, and app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 has no host argument so Node binds to all interfaces (dual-stack :: by default, which accepts network peers), letting an unauthenticated network peer reach the exec at tools.js:7 and tools.js:25 and read the git HEAD via tools.js:16-20. Two nuances: Node's default is `::` rather than literally `0.0.0.0`, and actual reachability depends on host firewall/NAT outside this file, which I could not check.
